author: san diego city wire
title: Brian W. Jones criticizes state budget while honoring local nonprofits
text:
Brian W. Jones, California State Senator representing the 40th District and former Senate Minority Leader, recently used his social media platform to highlight local nonprofit organizations and criticize state budget decisions.
On June 15, 2026, Jones acknowledged the work of community organizations in his district by posting: “Proud to recognize the distinguished nonprofits of the 40th District at our annual Nonprofit of the Year Reception. These organizations show up every single day for the people in our community who need them most and it was an honor to celebrate the work they do. A special https://t.co/Z8V9cdXVvi” .
Two days later, on June 17, 2026, Jones turned his attention to state fiscal policy with a critical assessment of Governor Gavin Newsom’s budget. He stated, “Newsom’s Last Budget. Same Failures. State spending grew 77 percent under Newsom while revenue could not keep up. He refuses to fully fund Prop 36 that 68 percent of voters passed. Small businesses are paying $662 million in interest on a pandemic debt he chose not to pay.”
In a subsequent post on June 17, Jones addressed legislative priorities and fiscal concerns: “Democrats want to raise taxes on software and businesses, delay healthcare cuts and spend more on homelessness while the LAO warns the numbers may not hold. California cannot keep kicking these decisions down the road. #FixCalifornia https://t.co/ZrcBavSMHT”
Jones has been active in public service through legislative efforts focused on education and veteran support ( official website ). Born into a military family in Austin, Texas, he has held seats in both the California State Assembly and State Senate. In addition to his legislative roles, Jones is married with three adult children and holds degrees from Grossmont College and San Diego State University.
summary: Brian W. Jones, California State Senator representing the 40th District and former Senate Minority Leader, recently used his social media platform to highlight local nonprofit organizations and criticize state budget decisions. Two days later, on June 17, 2026, Jones turned his attention to state fiscal policy with a critical assessment of Governor Gavin Newsom’s budget.
